marks.description: What the view draws, in drawing order.

layout.description:
How the view places vertex rows without positions: a diagram's blocks, or points on a plane
or the earth, gaps in the space's units.

ease.description: Seconds that changes ease over; 0.3 unless set.

title.description: Written at the view's top left, larger than the theme's text.

oneOf.description: Longitude and latitude in degrees, on a map or a globe.
Plane units with elevation: graphs and scenes the camera turns and tilts around.
The data's axis across, values up.
A sheet for diagrams: x right and y down in units, every length a unit.

Space.description:
The coordinate space a scene's positions are in: a name, or `{ plane | diagram | earth | plot:
options }`. A diagram is a flat sheet seen from straight above: y runs down, and every length is a
unit, a CSS pixel at zoom 0, except glow, halo, and pick radius. Only a diagram has ports, groups,
nets, orthogonal routes, and layouts.

projection.description: A flat map or a globe.

surface.description: The ground's color; the theme's surface unless set.

graticule.description: Whether lines of longitude and latitude cross the ground, in the theme's grid color.

daylight.description:
Lit by the sun as it stands this many seconds after the Unix epoch, plus the view's axis
coordinate when it shows one: night falls on the ground and what stands on it, down to the
theme's night. Lit evenly unless set.

atmosphere.description: Whether air glows around the globe, in the theme's atmosphere color, brighter where it is day.

Earth.description: The earth: positions are longitude and latitude in degrees.

oneOf.description: Web mercator.
A sphere.

Plane.description: A plane: positions are plane units.

oneOf.description: No grid.
Lines `pitch` units apart, thinned by tens as the view zooms out.

snap.description: Whether moved vertices snap to the dots.

oneOf.description: Dots `pitch` units apart; drags snap to them when `snap`.

Grid.description: A plane's or a diagram's grid: `"off"`, `{ lines: { pitch } }`, or `{ dots: { pitch, snap } }`.

Plot.description: A plot: x is the data's axis, y the values.

grid.description: Whether grid lines cross the plot at the ticks.

ticks.description:
Ticks at these values, each a value or `[value, label]`, their values written unless labeled;
round values unless set.

precision.description:
Decimals of fixed values, or of the significand of scientific and engineering ones; as many
as the ticks' step needs unless set.

Tick.description: A tick as written: a value, or `[value, label]`.

oneOf.description: Fixed decimals, scientific past a million or below a ten-thousandth.
Fixed decimals: `1500.0`.
A significand and a power of ten: `1.5e3`.
A significand and a power of ten that is a multiple of three: `1.5e3`, `150e-6`.

Format.description: How an axis writes its tick values.

Diagram.description:
A sheet for diagrams, flat and seen from straight above: the camera pans and zooms. Positions are
units with y down, and every length is a unit, a CSS pixel at zoom 0 (sizes, padding, ports,
strokes, text, and the theme's), except glow, halo, and pick radius. Zooming scales one fixed
picture. Only a diagram has ports, groups, nets, and orthogonal routes; it lays out blocks.

oneOf.description: Rows drawn as markers.
Rows drawn as strokes between two vertices.
Rows drawn as triangles between three vertices.
Rows drawn as lines along their paths, or on a plot through their samples.
Rows drawn as the areas their polygons cover.

Mark.description: One drawn table of a scene: `{ vertices | edges | faces | lines | areas: options }` as JSON.

position.description:
Each row's x and y. Without them, the point field `geometry` names places rows; rows without
either the scene's layout places.

geometry.description: The point field placing each row where `position` is not given; `geometry` unless set.

elevation.description:
Height above the ground: on the earth, a fraction of its radius. Not in a diagram, which is
flat.

radius.description: CSS pixels, or position units with `units`; units in a diagram.

size.description:
Width and height, for markers that are not round: CSS pixels, or position units with `units`;
units in a diagram, where a block without a size fits its label and ports.

ring.description: A ring around each row's marker in this color; a missing or transparent color draws none.

ports.description:
A port on each row for each reference field naming a net, which an `edges` mark of the net
table without ends draws. Diagrams only.

contains.description:
Makes each row a group: it holds the rows of `table` whose reference field names it, and is
drawn as a container around them, its label a title in its header. Diagrams only.

color.description: Each row's color; the theme's unless set.

visible.description: Whether each row is drawn and picked.

priority.description:
Each row's priority, from its data alone: what matters more draws on top, stays drawn as
a table too large to draw whole thins to the tiles in view, and is labeled first.

name.description: Tells two marks of one table apart across scenes, and names the mark in hits.

pick.description: Whether rows are hovered, clicked, and probed.

select.description: Whether a click selects a row.

drag.description: Whether pressing a row drags it instead of panning.

label.description: Each row's text: a text field, or a label's options.

shadow.description:
Whether each row casts a shadow onto the ground and onto faces, away from the theme's
light.

legend.description:
A legend of the colors at the view's bottom right, under this title: the colormap across
its domain, ticked; a cell for each category; or a swatch beside each name of a map's
`categories`. The color maps through a colormap with a domain or named categories; a
conditional's `otherwise` is read before its cases.

Vertices.description: Rows drawn as markers: points of a map, nodes of a graph, blocks of a diagram.

ExprNode.description: A value for every row of a mark: a constant, a field, view state, or arithmetic of them.

anyOf.description: A field's name, or a hex color when it starts with `#`.

of.description: The dataset and table the field is read from, joined by row id.

step.description: Reads a sampled field at its last frame without interpolating.

FieldNode.description: A field of each row: of the mark's own table, or of another dataset's table joined by row id.

color.description: A CSS color, such as `#ffb000` or `rebeccapurple`.

StateNode.description: What the view knows of each row.

State.description: What the view knows of each row.

MissingNode.description: A missing value: options that read one take the theme's.

WhenNode.description: The value of the first case whose condition holds, else `otherwise`.

IsNode.description: Whether a text field equals the text.

ContainsNode.description: Whether a text field holds the text, ignoring case: read by queries, which hold texts.

ScaleNode.description:
`value` mapped linearly onto the range `scale`, clamped: from its `domain`, else from the extent of
the values shown.

ColormapNode.description: `value` through `colormap`: from its `domain`, else from the extent of the values shown.

Colormap.description: Colors for a range of values: a catalog name, or your own colors.

anyOf.description: A CSS color, such as `#ffb000` or `rebeccapurple`.

prefixItems.description: A CSS color, such as `#ffb000` or `rebeccapurple`.

colors.description:
Colors blended in OKLab, each at its `[place, color]` from 0 to 1 or evenly between its
neighbors, as in a CSS gradient; a categorical map's, one per category.

categories.description: The categories' names, in order, for a legend: a categorical map's alone.

CustomColormap.description: Your own colormap: its kind, its colors, and for a categorical map its categories' names.

oneOf.description: Low to high.
Below and above a middle.
Around a circle: values wrap.
Distinct colors for distinct integers.

Size.description: A size: CSS pixels, or position units with `units`.

atLeast.description: CSS pixels it keeps at least, however far the view zooms out.

atMost.description: CSS pixels it keeps at most, however far the view zooms in.

Units.description: A size in position units, so it scales as the view zooms, kept within CSS pixels when given.

oneOf.description: A filled shape.
A block: a rectangle with rounded corners of `corner` CSS pixels, sized for diagrams.

corner.description: Corner radius, CSS pixels; 4 unless set.

oneOf.description: A shape's outline, filled to `fill` from 0 to 1: around a circle, up other shapes.

fill.description: How full each row's gauge is.

oneOf.description: A circle cut into slices, each as large as its value.

items.description: A CSS color, such as `#ffb000` or `rebeccapurple`.

hole.description: The hole in the middle, as a fraction of the radius.

oneOf.description: One of `images`, fitted in the marker's box; `index` picks which for each row.

A marker in WGSL: `source` defines `fn marker(f: MarkerFragment) -> MarkerColor`, reading up to
eight `inputs` as `f.input[i]`. It compiles once, when the view first draws it.

Marker.description:
How a vertex is drawn: a shape's name, `"block"`, or `{ shape | block | gauge | pie | icon | wgsl:
options }`.

oneOf.description: An ellipse: a circle when its width and height are equal.
A rectangle.
A rectangle with rounded corners.
A diamond.

Bitmap.description: RGBA texels, straight alpha, sRGB, rows top to bottom.

order.description: Its place among the ports on that side, from the top or the left; in declaration order unless set.

label.description: Its name, drawn beside it inside the marker.

output.description: Whether it drives the net its reference field names; an input unless set.

Port.description:
A vertex's port: where a net its reference field names meets it, on one side of its marker: a
side, or options. An output drives its net: layouts rank a net from its outputs, and its arrows
point away from them.

```
# use latkit::{Port, Side, Vertices};
let pumps = Vertices::of("plant", "Pump").port("in", Side::Left).port("out", Port::output(Side::Right));
```

oneOf.description: The left side.
The right side.
The top.
The bottom.

anyOf.description:
A row's text, placed beside, inside, or along what its mark draws, following it every frame: a
text field, or options. Labels that would overlap give way by priority; among equals, those
already shown keep their place. In a diagram a label is part of the drawing: it scales with the
zoom, fades out once too small to read, and shows wherever it fits its vertex.

```
# use latkit::{field, Label, Vertices};
let buses = Vertices::of("grid", "Bus").position("lon", "lat").label(Label::new("name").priority(field("kv")));
```

size.description: CSS pixels, or units in a diagram; the theme's font size unless set.

color.description: Each row's text color; the theme's text color unless set.

priority.description: Where labels would overlap, the higher shows; the mark's priority unless set.

maxWidth.description: How far a line runs before it wraps: CSS pixels, or units in a diagram.

font.description: The CSS font family list its texts are set in; the theme's font unless set.

max.description:
The most labels shown at once, those of highest priority among the rows in view; where they
would overlap, fewer.

ends.description: The reference fields naming each row's two vertices.

bends.description: A path field of points each row runs through between its ends.

route.description:
How each row runs between its ends; on the earth geodesic, elsewhere straight, unless set.
Orthogonal routes run around blocks, bends rounded; diagrams only.

arrows.description: Whether each row ends in an arrowhead at its second end; a net's at each input it reaches.

poles.description:
Draws each row as a pole from its own vertex down to the ground beneath it, on a plane or the
earth; it has no ends.

joins.description:
Draws each row as a net on a plane or the earth: it joins the vertex rows of `table` whose
reference field names it, as a star from their middle to each.

width.description: CSS pixels, or position units with `units`; units in a diagram.

flow.description:
Comets flowing along each row at this speed a second: CSS pixels, units in a diagram,
or position units where the theme's flow is in units; negative flows backward. A speed
that changes carries comets on from where they are.

Edges.description: Rows drawn as strokes between the vertices two reference fields name: branches, links, wires. In a diagram, a row without ends is a net: it joins every vertex port whose reference field names it.

oneOf.description: Straight across the screen.
Along the great circle, on the earth.

In horizontal and vertical runs around vertices, leaving and entering at their sides, bends
rounded. Diagrams only.

Route.description: How an edge runs between its ends.

corners.description:
The reference fields naming each row's three vertices. Without a color, a face blends the
colors of its corners.

Faces.description: Rows drawn as triangles between the vertices three reference fields name: meshes, surfaces, and fields interpolated across a network. Faces are lit from the camera, so a flat mesh seen from above shows its exact colors.

geometry.description: The path or polygon field each row runs along; `geometry` unless set. Not on a plot.

trace.description:
The sampled field each row traces across the data's axis, on a plot alone. A field not recorded
yet draws nothing until its first frame.

interpolation.description: How each row runs between its samples, on a plot.

or position units where the theme's flow is in units; negative flows backward. A speed

Lines.description: Rows drawn as lines: along a path field (roads, rivers, borders) or a polygon field's rings, outlining its areas; on a plot, through a sampled field's history across the data's axis, what a monitor shows. On the earth paths bend with the globe and stay whole across the antimeridian.

oneOf.description: Straight from each sample to the next.
Each value holds from the sample before it: steps rise at their samples' ends.
Each value holds until the next sample: steps rise at the next sample.

Interpolation.description: How a line runs between its samples.

geometry.description: The polygon field each row fills: one polygon's rings, or polygons. `geometry` unless set.

Areas.description: Rows drawn as the areas a polygon field holds: parcels, states, lakes, the land and water of a map. The view cuts each row's polygons into triangles once, off the frame when they are large; on the earth they bend with the globe and stay whole across the antimeridian. Outline areas with a [`Lines`](crate::Lines) mark of the same table, which draws their rings.

oneOf.description: Distances on the drawing follow distances in the graph.
Ranks along a direction, for flows and hierarchies.

Layout.description:
How the view places vertex rows without positions: a diagram's blocks, sized, or the points of a
plane or the earth, among the rows linked to them, gaps in the space's units: a name, or `{ stress
| layered: options }`. A place, once given, holds: rows added later are placed around the rest,
and [`View::arrange`](crate::View::arrange) lays every row out again.

Stress.description:
Stress majorization: each pair of vertices pulls toward its graph distance; then their boxes
part, keeping a quarter of the gap clear.

gap.description: Units between vertices of a rank.

Layered.description: Layered drawing: vertices in ranks, edges pointing along `flow`, and nets from their outputs.

oneOf.description: Toward the right.
Toward the left.
Toward the bottom.
Toward the top.

surface.description: The earth's ground, and a group's container.

grid.description: A plane's or a diagram's grid.

edge.description:
Edge color; `None` blends the colors of each edge's two vertices, and in a diagram takes the
text color.

shading.description: How much a face turned away from the camera darkens, 0 to 1.

text.description: Text: labels, axis ticks, and titles.

font.description: The CSS font family text is set in.

playhead.description: The line a plot draws at the shown coordinate.

missing.description: What a missing color reads as.

selected.description: The glow around selected rows; `None` glows in each row's own color.

glow.description: How far focus glows reach, CSS pixels.

dim.description: The opacity of rows outside a selection.

hoverScale.description: How much a hovered vertex sized in CSS pixels grows.

flow.description: How comets flowing along edges and lines look.

edgeSpacing.description:
In a diagram, distance between the lanes of edges joining the same two vertices, and between
parallel orthogonal wires, which keep twice it apart.

laneBow.description:
Elsewhere, how far edges joining the same two vertices bow apart: each lane by this fraction
of the edge's length at its middle. A bow is part of the drawing, so zooming never moves it.

arrow.description: How far an arrowhead reaches past its edge's width.

halo.description: CSS pixels of background around label text.

groupPadding.description: Distance between a group's members and its outline.

shadow.description: How marks that cast shadows cast them.

atmosphere.description: The air glowing around the globe, where the earth has an atmosphere.

night.description: How bright the earth's night side stays where it is lit by daylight, 0 to 1.

base.description: The theme these options change; dark unless set.

Theme.description:
Colors and sizes marks take where their options read nothing, and the look of focus and motion: a
base theme's name, or options over one (`base`, dark unless set). Lengths are CSS pixels; in a
diagram they are units, except `glow` and `halo`.

color.description: A comet's color; its alpha is how strongly a comet covers its stroke.

length.description: How far a comet's tail trails its head.

width.description: How wide a comet's head is, CSS pixels, or units in a diagram; never narrower than its stroke.

units.description:
Whether comets are part of the drawing: their spacing, length, and each row's flow in position
units, degrees on the earth, so they zoom with the view and stay where they are on their lines.
Otherwise they keep their size and speed on screen, and slide along their lines as it zooms.

Flow.description:
How comets flowing along edges and lines look: each a round head, brightest at its middle, trailing
a tail that thins and fades.

color.description: What a shadow darkens toward; its alpha is how dark a shadow at contact gets.

light.description: The direction toward the light, fixed in the world: shadows fall away from it.

softness.description: How much a shadow spreads per unit of a caster's height: the light's size.

lift.description: CSS pixels flat marks cast from, as if raised.

Shadow.description: How marks that cast shadows cast them onto the ground and onto faces.

pan.description: Dragging the background moves the camera.

zoom.description:
What zooms: the wheel and pinching, or the wheel only with Control or Meta held (as a
trackpad's pinch sends it), leaving the plain wheel to scroll the page; or nothing.

turn.description: Dragging with the secondary button, or with Shift, turns and tilts a map or plane.

hover.description:
The row the user points at glows. It is hovered either way: events tell it, and `hovered()`
reads it.

pickRadius.description: CSS pixels around the pointer that picks reach; touch reaches 8 more.

selectBox.description:
Dragging with Shift selects the rows in a box, instead of turning; a Shift click still toggles
its row.

connect.description:
Dragging from a port, from a vertex with Alt, or an edge off its end draws a connection,
told as [`Event::Connect`](crate::Event).

delete.description: Delete and Backspace tell [`Event::Delete`](crate::Event) with the selection.

cycle.description:
Clicking again where nothing moved selects the next row under the point, nearest first, so
rows drawn over one another can each be selected.

press.description:
Seconds a touch or a pen held still asks for a menu, as the secondary button does; zero never
does.

motion.description:
How much the view moves on its own: eases, flights, coasting, orbits, label fades, comets, and
what reads `elapsed()`.

Controls.description:
How a view answers the pointer and keyboard, and how much it moves on its own: a preset, or options
over the defaults. Each mark says whether its rows pick, select, and drag; these say what the view
itself does.

oneOf.description: The wheel, pinching, and the keys.

Pinching and the keys, and the wheel only with Control or Meta held, as a trackpad's pinch
sends it: the plain wheel scrolls the page.
Nothing.
As the platform asks: reduced where the user asked their system for less motion.
Every motion.

Only what the user moves: changes apply at once, flights jump, nothing coasts or orbits,
labels show without fading, and comets and what reads `elapsed()` hold still.

Motion.description: How much a view moves on its own.

Data.description: A dataset: its name and the patch that builds it.

oneOf.description: Names the axis sampled fields are recorded over, such as `time` in `s`.

fields.description: Fields by name, in the order written.

additionalProperties.description: A field's values: an array of one kind of value; a reference naming another table's rows by id; or a slice of a binary file beside the document.

oneOf.description: Replaces a table with these rows and fields, or adds it.

fields.description: Fields by name, in the order written.

additionalProperties.description: A field's values: an array of one kind of value; a reference naming another table's rows by id; or a slice of a binary file beside the document.

oneOf.description:
Writes fields for these rows: rows with known ids change, others are added, and fields left
out keep their values.
Removes the rows with these ids.

fields.description: Fields by name, in the order written.

additionalProperties.description: A field's values: an array of one kind of value; a reference naming another table's rows by id; or a slice of a binary file beside the document.

oneOf.description:
Records a frame at each axis coordinate of `at`: for each field, a value per row at every
coordinate, frame-major; of every row, or of the rows `ids` names, the rest holding their last
values.
Forgets every sampled field's frames before axis coordinate `before`.

Holds a run of sampled field `field`'s entries of level `level`, numbered from `first`: at
level 0 frames, each a coordinate in `at` and a value per row in `values`; at level `k` buckets
of `8^k` frames, each its first and last frame's coordinates, and each row's least value over
each bucket, then each row's greatest. Null is missing.

Change.description: One change of a patch, named by the method that makes it.

Ids.description: Row ids: numbers or texts (null leaves a reference unwired), or `{count}` naming rows 0..count.

Id.description: A row's id: a whole number from 0, or a text. A number above 2^53 - 1 is written as its decimal text, which names the same row.

Value.description: One value: a number, boolean, text, or geometry; null, or an empty geometry, is missing.

Geometry.description: A point `[x, y]` (a third coordinate is read past), or a list of geometries one level shallower: a path, its parts, or polygons.

Dtype.description: How a slice's bytes hold values: little endian; `bool` a byte each, nonzero true.

ids.description:
The rows read, in this order unless sorted; every row unless set. Ids that name no row are
passed over.

filter.description: Keeps the rows it is true for.

sort.description:
Keys to sort by, each after those before it; rows a key reads nothing for come last, and rows
all keys order alike keep their order.

limit.description: The most rows read; a limit picks them in linear time before sorting only those.

select.description: Fields to read by name: a field as it is, anything else as numbers. Every field unless set.

at.description: The axis coordinate sampled fields are read at; their last frame unless set.

Query.description: The rows of a table to read back, run through the expressions marks draw with.

oneOf.description: Least first.
Greatest first.

Order.description: Which way a sort runs; rows a key reads nothing for come last either way.

center.description:
Longitude, latitude, and elevation on the earth; x, y, and elevation on a plane or a
diagram. In JSON, `[x, y]` looks at the ground.

zoom.description: On the earth the web mercator level; elsewhere, log₂ of pixels per unit.

pitch.description: Degrees from looking straight down, up to 75; 0 in a diagram.

bearing.description: Degrees clockwise from north, or from up on a plane; 0 in a diagram.

anyOf.description:
On the earth, a plane, or a diagram: the point looked at and turned about, how far in, and how
tilted and turned. A diagram is always seen from straight above, upright.

y.description: The value range shown, or none to fit what is in view.

anyOf.description: On a plot: the axis range across, and the value range up, or none to fit the values in view.

oneOf.description: Everything drawn.
These rows.
Brings this row into view, keeping the zoom.
The box from `min` to `max`: x, y, and elevation.

ids.description: The rows' ids in the table.

Rows.description: Rows of one table in a dataset, by id: what a view selects, fits, and tells as sets of rows.

id.description: The row's id in the table.

Row.description: A row of a table in a dataset. It survives any change that keeps the names and the id.

bytes.description:
Bytes the data every view of the `Gpu` draws may take on the GPU: its pages, and each view's
rows. A view draws a table too large for its share through the tiles the camera asks for, so
what it draws always fits; pages no view draws stay cached in the room left, the least
recently drawn going first. By default half the device's largest storage buffer. The pool of
pages grows as data needs it, and never shrinks: set the budget before data draws.

uploadPerFrame.description: Bytes uploaded per frame at most; larger data streams in over frames.

Budget.description: How much GPU memory latkit uses.

scale.description: Pixels per CSS pixel: views lay out `size / scale` CSS pixels; 1 unless set.

panels.description: Each view's panel of the picture, `[x, y, width, height]` as fractions; the whole by default.

transparent.description: Whether alpha is kept where the themes' backgrounds would be.

deadline.description: Seconds a picture, or a video frame, may take; 30 unless set.

elapsed.description: A still's effect time in seconds, where elapsed time and flowing comets read it.

oneOf.description: A row was clicked.
A row was double clicked, or Enter pressed on the row the keys point at.

hits.description: What lies under the point, nearest first.

oneOf.description:
The secondary button clicked, or the menu key pressed: what lies under the trigger's point,
for a menu of what to do with it.

phase.description: Whether the drag starts, moves, or ends.

hit.description: The row dragged, as it was hit.

position.description:
Where the row goes, in the space's coordinates: where it was hit, moved as the pointer moved
since the press, at the depth the drag started; a vertex keeps where it was grabbed. On a
diagram's dots when its grid snaps.

oneOf.description:
A row of a draggable mark follows the pointer: the drag starts once the pointer moves a few
pixels from where it pressed the row.

from.description: The end it was drawn from: for an edge, the end that stayed.

to.description: The vertex it was released over, if any.

edge.description: The edge whose other end was dragged, which `to` replaces.

oneOf.description:
A connection was drawn with [`Controls::connect`](crate::Controls): from a port, a vertex
with Alt held, or an edge whose end was dragged off it.
Delete or Backspace with rows selected and [`Controls::delete`](crate::Controls) on.

hit.description: The row now pointed at; `None` once it left every row.

oneOf.description: What the user points at changed: [`View::hovered`](crate::View::hovered).

trigger.description: How the user changed it; `None` when the data dropped rows from it.

oneOf.description: The selection changed: [`View::selection`](crate::View::selection).

The camera moved by a gesture, a fit, a flight, coasting, or an orbit:
[`View::camera`](crate::View::camera).

What the last frame stood in for changed; nothing once it is complete:
[`View::complete`](crate::View::complete).

Something failed, told once. A mark its data no longer fits also lists in
[`View::failures`](crate::View::failures).

ViewEvent.description:
What happened in a view, for the application to act on. Drain them with
[`View::events`](crate::View::events).

mark.description: The name of the mark that drew it, when it has one: what tells two marks of one table apart.

point.description:
The point of the row nearest the probe, CSS pixels from the top left: a vertex's or a port's
middle, the nearest point of a stroke or a triangle.

position.description: That point in the space's coordinates: x, y, and elevation.

distance.description: CSS pixels from the probe to the row.

port.description: The port hit, when a vertex's port was.

sample.description: The sample hit, when a line tracing a sampled field was.

Hit.description: A row under a point, as the frame drew it.

id.description: The row's id in the table.

Row.description: A row of a table in a dataset. It survives any change that keeps the names and the id.

Id.description: A row's id: a whole number from 0, or a text. A number above 2^53 - 1 is written as its decimal text, which names the same row.

frame.description: The frame, numbered from the first ever recorded.

Sample.description: A sample of a traced field: its frame, the axis coordinate it was recorded at, and its value.

point.description: CSS pixels from the top left.

Trigger.description:
Where, with what keys, and with what the user acted. For keys, the point is the row they point
at, else the pointer, else the view's middle.

oneOf.description: A mouse or a trackpad.
A pen.
A finger: picks reach 8 CSS pixels farther.
The keys.
The pointer moved far enough to drag.
The pointer moved.
The pointer let go, or the drag was cancelled.

port.description: The port, by the reference field naming its net.

End.description: A vertex a connection ends at, and its port when it has the one the connection meets.

ids.description: The rows' ids in the table.

Rows.description: Rows of one table in a dataset, by id: what a view selects, fits, and tells as sets of rows.

center.description:
Longitude, latitude, and elevation on the earth; x, y, and elevation on a plane or a
diagram. In JSON, `[x, y]` looks at the ground.

zoom.description: On the earth the web mercator level; elsewhere, log₂ of pixels per unit.

pitch.description: Degrees from looking straight down, up to 75; 0 in a diagram.

bearing.description: Degrees clockwise from north, or from up on a plane; 0 in a diagram.

anyOf.description:
On the earth, a plane, or a diagram: the point looked at and turned about, how far in, and how
tilted and turned. A diagram is always seen from straight above, upright.

y.description: The value range shown, or none to fit what is in view.

anyOf.description: On a plot: the axis range across, and the value range up, or none to fit the values in view.

Waiting.description: Work under way a frame stands in for: pages uploading or tables not yet built from them (`data`); layouts, routes, lanes, shapes, tiles, or pyramids (`derived`); a label placement or texts not yet set (`labels`); a fit due or being measured (`fit`); row regions laid out again, segment counts, or a transition beginning (`marks`). Empty once a frame is complete.

Failure.description: What failed: its `code`, the message, and for invalid input the `path` to the part, such as `marks[2].vertices.color`.

drawn.description:
Rows every mark draws: every row of a table drawn whole, the rows of the tiles in view of one
drawn through tiles.

draws.description: Draw calls the last frame recorded, shadows and labels with the marks.

instances.description:
Instances the last frame's draws drew: points, segments, triangles, glyphs; at most, for
segments the GPU culls.

tiles.description: Fetched tiles the view draws, of every tile source.

tilesLoading.description: Tiles being fetched or decoded, of every tile source.

uploading.description: Bytes of data waiting to upload.

resident.description: Bytes of data pages on the GPU, for every view of its `Gpu`.

budget.description: Bytes the GPU's [`Budget`](crate::Budget) lets data take.

waiting.description:
The work under way the last frame stood in for; nothing when it drew everything as the data,
scene, and camera say: see [`View::complete`](crate::View::complete).

cpuMs.description: Milliseconds the last frame took to record on the CPU.

gpuMs.description:
Milliseconds the GPU takes on a frame: the median of the last frames it measured; 0 where the
device cannot measure.

Stats.description: What a view does each frame.

written.description: Bytes written besides pages: uniforms, programs, label runs, the selection, textures.

evaluated.description: Rows whose channels the GPU evaluated.

readbacks.description:
Reads back from the GPU: probes, queries, fits, label placements, segment counts, pictures;
not the frame timer's, which only some devices have.

jobs.description:
Jobs handed out: layouts, routes, lanes, triangulations, pyramids, tiles; to the host's
workers, or done at once without a host.

texts.description: Label texts the host was asked to set.

Work.description: What a [`Gpu`](crate::Gpu) did since it was made; subtract two for what happened between.

span.description: The first and last coordinates its sampled fields hold.

Description.description:
What a dataset holds: its tables, their rows and fields, and the axis its sampled fields are
recorded over and span.

TableDescription.description: A table described: its rows, and its fields by name.

span.description: The first and last coordinates a sampled field holds.

FieldDescription.description: A field described: what it holds, the table a reference names, the coordinates samples span.

oneOf.description: Numbers.
Booleans.
Texts.
`[x, y]` points.
Paths of points.
Parts: the rings of a polygon, or the paths of a multi-path.
Polygons of rings.
Rows of another table, by id.
Numbers sampled over the data's axis.

bytes.description:
Bytes the data every view of the `Gpu` draws may take on the GPU: its pages, and each view's
rows. A view draws a table too large for its share through the tiles the camera asks for, so
what it draws always fits; pages no view draws stay cached in the room left, the least
recently drawn going first. By default half the device's largest storage buffer. The pool of
pages grows as data needs it, and never shrinks: set the budget before data draws.

uploadPerFrame.description: Bytes uploaded per frame at most; larger data streams in over frames.

Budget.description: How much GPU memory latkit uses.

Value.description: A value read from a dataset: a number (`null` when not finite), boolean, or text; a geometry as nested `[x, y]` points; a reference as the id of the row it names.
